To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have isolated and partially purified a membrane-associated lytic toxin (M-CTX) from the plasma membranes prepared from a highly lytic LAK cell line (A-LAK) and a LGL leukemia (CRL-NC-16) that functions in the absence Ca2+ to induce apoptosis and massive membrane blebing in a wide panel of target cell types.
A novel plasma membrane-associated cytotoxic factor has been isolated from highly purified lymphocyte-activated killer (LAK) cells.
we have identified and partially characterized a novel cytolytically active protein (M-CTX) from highly purified A-LAK cells and a LGL leukemia.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the isolation, characterization, and identification of a novel lytic factor isolated and purified from the plasma membrane-associated fraction of highly enriched LAK cells.
the identification of novel cytolytic factors isolated from highly purified A-LAK cells.
the characterization and isolation of a novel plasma-membrane-associated lytic factor (M-CTX) from highly purified A-LAK cells and a large granulated NK cell leukemia (CRNK16).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the M-CTX is a novel plasma membrane- and not granule-associated lytic factor that is not a PFP or a TNF-alpha or an LT or an IFN-gamma, and which induces target cell death by an apoptotic pathway.
M-CTX is not a pore-forming protein, but rather a novel plasma membrane associated toxin.
the M-CTX is a novel plasma membrane- associated cytotoxic factor that is distinct from perforin and other known cytolytic molecules.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the M-CTX is a novel cytolytically active factor that has the potential to be used as a novel therapeutic agent against cancer.

we have identified and partially characterized a novel membrane-associated lytic toxin (M-CTX) that is distinct from perforin (PFP) and other previously characterized cytolytic factors (e.g., TNF-alpha, IFN-gamma, and LT) and that may represent an important component of the A-LAK cell lytic repertoire.

we have isolated and partially characterized a novel membrane-associated cytotoxic toxin (M-CTX) that is physically distinct from perforin and that may be involved in contact-mediated killing of target cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the A-LAK cells have a plasma membrane associated lytic factor that can lyse target cells in 4 hours.
there is a plasma membrane-associated lytically active molecule that is not perforin, and that it may represent a hereto-fore undescribed toxin that could be involved in contact-mediated cytolysis.
we identified a new cytolytic factor, and we are now trying to understand how this cytolytic factor is made, how it kills cells, and whether it is involved in killing tumor cells.
